summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, 13.0% of firms in transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) answered yes to whether they used AI in the last two weeks, against a prior period figure of 7.9%. The question was first asked in September 2023, and the Bureau suppresses some values, marked S. That is the only measured adoption figure in this material, and it describes a sector where most firms still report no AI use in the survey window.

Where AI is deployed, the sources split between vehicles and back-office operations. Aurora describes self-driving freight powered by the Aurora Driver, built with hardware and software it says is backed by verifiable AI, and quotes a fleet partner on a hybrid model combining professional drivers with the Aurora Driver on runs between Fort Worth and El Paso, plus integration into the Volvo VNL Autonomous. Samsara describes a connected operations platform used by 20,000+ operations, with AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, drowsiness detection and equipment management, and states that 380,000+ accidents have been prevented. C.H. Robinson frames its managed solutions as a move from managing logistics to autonomous logistics orchestration, where the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes and improves across every shipment, and runs an AI assistant on its site.

Maritime and aviation show the same pattern of vendor-led deployment under regulatory supervision. Wärtsilä says it uses AI-driven predictive analytics among the tools helping customers decarbonise. The IMO adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, a goal-based framework intended to ensure autonomous ships are designed, constructed, operated and certified to safety and environmental standards equivalent to conventional ships, currently voluntary guidance and designed to facilitate a future transition into a mandatory instrument. The IMO states that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely controlled, though trials have shown larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and it expects MASS to evolve gradually with only some functions automated at first and crew on board. Airbus describes a decarbonised, connected and autonomous future for aerospace, working with an innovation ecosystem and digitised operations. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out its vision for safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, provides an action plan for its AI Programme, and is a living document to be amended once a year.

Safety evidence is where the sources are most concrete. Waymo's safety page states it was born as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009 and served the first of many fully autonomous rides in 2015, that it has built a comprehensive safety program to guide testing and development, and that it supports the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy by advancing Safer Vehicles and Safer Speeds through research and deployment of its fully autonomous ride-hailing service, alongside the Vision Zero Network campaign to eliminate traffic fatalities and severe injuries. Aurora's quoted partners describe safety and efficiency benefits, better driver lives through handling lengthier and less desirable routes, and confidence from consistent performance over millions of autonomous miles. Samsara's accident-prevention figure is the clearest quantified operational claim in the material.

Money and vendor concentration sit with the autonomy platforms, the telematics and computer-vision suppliers, the freight brokers, and the maritime and aerospace equipment makers. This site's curated points name Aurora and Kodiak as pure-play autonomous trucking platforms operating Level 4 freight on commercial highway corridors, Samsara and Mobileye in fleet telematics and driver-assist vision, C.H. Robinson in freight matching and dynamic pricing, Wärtsilä and Maersk in maritime, Airbus and Boeing in aviation, and Palantir as a tracked enterprise AI platform used by airlines and rail operators for fleet and crew optimization. The American Trucking Associations is described as the industry body tracking policy and adoption for autonomous freight and AI logistics, with more than 37,000 members and a federation of 50 state trucking associations. This site also catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, including vision-language-action models, refreshed daily.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material points to a sector where measured adoption remains a minority position at 13.0% per the Census Bureau, while the visible deployments are concentrated in a few well-capitalised operators and their suppliers. The regulatory posture differs sharply by mode. Aviation AI passes through EASA's roadmap and the FAA's innovation work, which this site's curated points describe as the regulatory record for AI flight systems, automated risk management and eVTOL certification, with nothing flying commercially without them. Maritime autonomy now has the IMO's MASS Code, voluntary at adoption and intended to become mandatory. Trucking policy is tracked by the American Trucking Associations. The practical read is that the operational case in this material rests on safety and efficiency claims from vendors and operators, the strongest quantified evidence being Samsara's accident-prevention figure and Waymo's published safety methodology, and that any deployment touching vehicles, vessels or aircraft will be gated by a regulator before it is gated by ROI.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The World of AI catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each model's licence, download count and release date and refreshing the list daily. The site says the catalogue is built from the Hugging Face Hub's public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. It gives 2026-09-28 as the date the page was last verified. The same page describes the wider site as an atlas of artificial intelligence covering what the law says, who is suing whom and what the words mean, rebuilt daily from primary sources.
